doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

chapter: Teenage obsession and the record store
title: Opening and listening to WIBG on a transistor radio
summary: Rowe introduces Gordon; they trade memories of late-night transistor radio and WIBG's mix of British Invasion, Motown and pop on one Top 100.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive. I’m going to be joined by Christian Goodwillie who is the Director of Special Collections at Hamilton College. I’m very pleased to have Jerry Gordon with us today. And I’m going to introduce you as a man who channeled his early obsession for music into a number of very productive projects and is valuable for musicians and listeners. How is that for a mouthful?
Well thank you, Monk, you made me presentable, I really appreciate that.
I think you and I have a number of things in common and one of them would have been staying up late listening to a transistor radio.

Absolutely. And Philadelphia, the station when I was a young teen, 13 years old, was WIBG. And yes, I was listening on the transistor and the story I like to tell everybody about WIBG was it was a station and an era where you could hear the British Invasion, Motown, Dean Martin, and Slim Harpo, all within the same hour and all next to each other on the WIBG Top 100. So that was my start.

I remember the same thing. You know Mitch Miller followed by Elvis Presley. And you didn’t have to choose what’s my favorite kind of music because it was all there and you could have multiple favorites.
